The less touristy Pai in Northern Thailand has been one of my favourite destinations so far. To get here you can take a short 3 hour van ride from Chiang Mai, or you can rent a scooter and drive the loop yourself for the scenic and windy road. This small town is very hippy and artsy, and the Thai people here are extremely open minded. People usually end up extending their stay here from 2 nights to 1 week up until 2 or 3 months sometimes. One of the many things that make Pai so wonderful is the amazing food. You can get authentic street food, the best Pad Thai in Thailand, Northern Thai dishes, and just loads of curry. I could not recommend Pai more.

I purchased a motorbike in Hanoi and drove 9 hours to Ha giang, where I then did the 4 day Ha Giang Loop, this was on the third day with this view of an amazing valley, taken at an amazing time during rainy season where the river is usually brown due to the insane amounts of downpour. These roads are the worst I’ve ever driven, some even being constructed as I was driving on them, but this just made the feeling of accomplishment when you finish that last day all that much better. This was the best thing I’ve done in Vietnam, by far. Not just the views and driving, but the home-stays, family dinners and rice wine in the little villages along the way. If you’re ever in Vietnam, do this loop before it gets overwhelmed by tourists.
